blocker: Frame size now matches at 0xfc (target and mine both 'sub sp, sp, #0xfc'), and the object is 2868 B vs 2836 B. The diff is still dominated by instruction scheduling, not logic: the largest single mismatch cluster is 244 lines covering 0x2CC800-0x2CC9xx (the base-ctor prologue plus the first ~0x2cc of the body).  In detail: (1) the target's prologue zero-fills NpcInitParam with 'mov r2,#0; mov r3,r2; mov r4,r2; mov ip,#1; stm r1,{r2,r3,r4}' while every source shape tried (default-argument ctor, plain zero ctor, aggregate, 5-argument ctor) leaves either a 16-byte literal copy plus __aeabi_memcpy or a different register order; the target's register-fill is an allocator artifact of the base call's argument needs.  (2) The target builds the NpcInitParam and calls the base ctor as its FIRST action, while armcc emits the FixedSafeString setup first (mine: 'add r0,fp,#0xc8; sub sp,#0xfc; ldm r0,{r0-r3}'), so the whole first 0x40 bytes are transposed.  (3) The target's bulk state-table fill at 0x2CCA7C stores the same 8-byte member-pointer pair with a 16-byte stride into mEnter/mExec and splits the mExit fill odd/even; my flat 22-entry loop is closer but still not the same loop.  (4) The three saved stack pointers at 0xbc/0xc0/0xe4 (0xe4 is a pointer into this, dereferenced at 0x2CD1CC as [r0,#0xb1]) are not yet modelled as named locals, and their absence shifts register allocation throughout.
helped: The stdarg fix was decisive: with a pointer va_list the model-path block compiles, the frame grew from 0x7c to 0xe4 and then to 0xfc at -O3, matching the target exactly, and the FixedSafeString<64> construction inlines into six field writes per object as the target does.  Two traps cost most of the time and are worth passing on: armcc 4.1 silently CRASHES (exit 5, no diagnostics) when a variadic member function is defined inside a class template, and its shipped struct-typed va_list makes the first variadic function in a TU fail with #928, so format() must live in the non-template base class and va_list must be a pointer.  vec3.h was used unchanged for the position table and the point->pos copies.  statemgr.h's StateMgrT layout was confirmed field for field (mNum +6, mOwner +0x14, mEnter +0x18, mExec +0x1c, mExit +0x20, 0x24 bytes, s32 at +0x984); only mNames[2] is wrong (it is a Buffer<FixedSafeString<24>>).  The Player ctor gave the house idioms for the two-vptr base and 'new (nt) T()' with the nothrow argument left in r1.  Also confirmed: armcc reuses the stack slot of two non-overlapping FixedSafeString locals unless both are declared in the constructor's outer scope - which is what the target does (0x14 and 0x68).
